title: Mass VPN outage — finance team can't work
description: Since 09:30 this morning, half of the finance team can't connect to the VPN. It's affecting the budgeting processes.

worklogs.description: Compiled the list of affected users: 12 finance + 3 accounting = 15 people.
An abnormal spike in failed-auth was observed on the VPN gateway monitoring panel.
A 'token cache invalidation' error was identified in the RADIUS server logs.
The RADIUS service was controlled-restarted and the cache was cleared.
The connection of all 15 affected users was verified one by one.
A post-mortem document was prepared, recording the root cause + prevention steps.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: Urgent! The whole team has been unable to connect for 30 minutes. We have an 11:00 meeting with the CFO for the budget revision, please intervene.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Hi, I've picked this up right away. I'm prioritizing it. First: how many people are affected, and are they all getting the same error message? Could you send a screenshot from one or two users?

comments.author: customer
comments.message: Around 15 people, all getting 'Authentication failed'. I've attached 3 screenshots.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Thank you. The error is clear — there's an issue with the authentication infrastructure, not something caused by a single user. I've immediately started an escalation with the network and security teams. This is a major incident, and I'm handling it as a P1. Estimated fix: within 30 minutes. I'm tracking it live as well, and I'll update you here as things progress.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: On the RADIUS dashboard, the auth failed graph spiked starting at 09:25. I'm looking into it together with the network team (Murat). We suspect a token cache invalidation bug — an upgrade was done last week.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Update: Root cause identified — the authentication token cache on the RADIUS server is corrupted (a bug following last week's upgrade). To clear the cache, the service will be controlled-restarted within 5 minutes. Existing connections won't be affected during the restart, but anyone trying to connect anew may see a 2-3 minute delay.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: RADIUS has been restarted. Please test one user's VPN connection and let me know. 1 person out of all 15 is enough — if it works, it'll apply to the others too.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: Ali tested it and connected! A couple more people tried, and it works. We made it to the CFO meeting. Thank you so much; we never imagined it could be this fast with you.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Glad to hear it. The whole team made the 11:00 meeting, and that's what really matters. I'm preparing a detailed post-mortem on this for prevention steps. I'll share it in the coming days — I'm going to recommend adding an automatic smoke-test for RADIUS upgrades. Your urgent response and clear communication also sped up the process; thank you.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Post-mortem: the token-cache bug is documented in the vendor's knowledge base (workaround: restart). For a permanent fix, a migration to the 8.5.2 patch will be planned — tracked as RFC-1142.

resolutionNote: A token cache invalidation bug (post-upgrade) was identified on the RADIUS auth server. The cache was cleared via a controlled-restart of the service, and the connection of the 15 affected users returned to normal. Total impact duration ~50 minutes. A post-mortem document was prepared, and a migration to the 8.5.2 patch was planned.

csat.comment: We got very fast and clear support during a crisis. The communication was excellent — we were kept informed at every stage. Thank you.
